To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the tick’s salivarium is a flexible tube, (ii) the salivarium is opened/closed by muscles attached to it, (iii) saliva is pumped into the salivarium, (iv) saliva is pumped out through the salivarium by a mechanism that involves the salivary pump, and (v) the saliva is pumped out of the salivarium into the host skin.
the salivarium is closed during the blood meal uptake and opens during saliva secretion.
the salivarium is a complex structure with a complex mechanism of action, which is not fully known.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of blood meal uptake and saliva outflow in hard ticks, and how these two processes are coordinated during tick feeding.
the mechanism of saliva and blood meal acquisition and the possible role of saliva in the blood meal uptake.
the mechanisms that underlie the tick’s ability to feed and transmit pathogens to and from its hosts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tick’s mouthpart mechanism is an elegant and complex system, which enables ticks to perform a variety of functions that are critical to the success of their parasitic lives.
the tick’s feeding apparatus is an extremely complex system that is highly adapted to the specific needs of the tick’s life cycle and its feeding strategy.
the tick’s mouthpart functions are highly complex, and their precise mechanisms are not yet fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our model is a new insight into tick’s blood-feeding mechanism and it will be useful for further studies on tick saliva and saliva-associated molecules.
our 3-D model of the tick feeding apparatus is a useful tool to better understand the mechanisms of blood meal uptake and saliva secretion in hard ticks.
the tick’s mouthpart functions in a highly orchestrated way to ensure blood meal uptake and saliva secretion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tick saliva and blood meal uptake occur at different locations in the mouthpart and are separated by a mechanical barrier, which is a unique mechanism in arthropods.
the tick’s mouthpart functions are orchestrated by the salivarium, which is a unique organ in arthropods.
the tick’s mouth is not a simple, passive conduit for blood meal uptake and saliva secretion, but a complex structure that can actively manipulate the flow of blood and saliva.
